Harden update parsing against additive Telegram Bot API changes.

A single `getUpdates` batch with one unparseable update would crash the entire batch and leave the polling offset un-advanced, causing the caller to re-fetch and re-crash on the same update indefinitely. Observed in production as a 5616-event/9-hour outage triggered by a Bot API 7.0 `blockquote` entity hitting a strict enum coercion.

### Fixed

- `MessageEntityType` now includes `blockquote` (Bot API 7.0) and `expandable_blockquote` (Bot API 7.2) cases that were missing from the enum.

### Added

- `MessageEntity::tryCreate()` — tolerant factory that returns `null` when Telegram emits an entity type the SDK does not yet recognize. The strict `MessageEntity::create()` is preserved for callers that want to fail loud.
- `GetUpdatesResponse::$parseErrors` — public array of throwables captured from per-update parse failures. Callers can iterate this to report failures (e.g. to Sentry) without losing the rest of the batch.

### Changed

- `TextMessage::createEntities()` now skips entity types the SDK does not recognize via `MessageEntity::tryCreate()`, so a future additive Bot API change cannot poison the surrounding message parse.
- `GetUpdatesResponse::init()` now isolates per-update parse failures: the throwable is recorded in `$parseErrors` and a `GenericUpdate(update_id)` is substituted so the caller can advance the polling offset past the bad update. Updates with no integer `update_id` are dropped from the result entirely.
